title: A screen can show the column grid you are designing to
goal: Real UI is laid out on columns: twelve columns with a gutter, or four on a phone. Photonz can arrange things in a stack or a grid container, but there is no way to put a column guide behind a whole screen and see whether the pieces on it land on the columns. A screen gets an optional column overlay, set by its number of columns, its gutter and its margin, and dragging a layer on that screen pulls to the column edges the way dragging already pulls to other layers.
notes:
BLOCKED on its decision card until the user answers, because it puts something new on screen. From the ui-grid mock, and named as unbuilt in the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-03-auto-layout.json: the mock layout grid is a column overlay you eyeball against, not a container that positions what it holds, and only the container was built. Ships behind next-frames since only a screen carries one, or its own Next flag if the runner prefers; either way on by default in Next. The overlay is chrome, not content: it belongs with the canvas overlays in CanvasView, not in the render path, so it can never reach an export. Whether it also snaps is the card question, and the answer decides whether LayerSnapping is touched at all.

Decision answered on 2026-09-05: option b, columns you can see AND stick to. The user picked the snapping over the draw-only overlay, having turned down guides that pulled at a drag once before, so the mitigation they chose with it is load bearing: it only ever pulls on a screen with an overlay switched on, and a screenshot or a plain canvas must feel exactly as it does today. Test that explicitly.

Triage 2026-09-05: there is now a second grid in the queue, a-grid-you-can-switch-on-that-thins-and-thickens at p1, asked for by the user the same morning. That one is a canvas wide grid you build against, spacing based, belonging to the canvas; this one is a per screen column guide with a count, a gutter and a margin. They must read as one idea rather than two grids with different words, and the audit for whichever lands second has to say how a person tells them apart.
acceptance: A screen can be given a column overlay with a column count, a gutter and a margin, all typed
The columns draw faintly behind everything on that screen, at every zoom, and never appear in an export or a copied picture

Dragging a layer on a screen that has an overlay switched on pulls to the column edges, with a short line showing which column it caught, matching the layer to layer snapping already in the app rather than being a second idea beside it
Holding Command drags free of the columns, the same key that already frees a drag from the other snapping
A screen with no overlay, a plain canvas and a screenshot all drag exactly as they do today, so nothing new tugs at a redline
The overlay can be switched off and on for a screen without losing its numbers, and switching it off stops the pulling too
Each screen keeps its own settings, and a document with none of them is byte for byte what it was
Ships behind next-frames, since only a screen carries one. To see it: open Photonz Next, draw a screen, set twelve columns, and drag a box across it
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
